sections.sectionText: This is a 3rd semester course aiming to review basic Portuguese structures and introduce more advanced ones in a contextualized manner through the use of a variety of texts to help students develop grammatically sound oral and written communication in Portuguese. The course is based on texts and is divided into 26 units, each presenting a short story or crônica. Each text explores language in 3 different ways: 1) pre-reading exercises to encourage students to converse, 2) writing activities to be done individually or in small groups, and 3) grammar and vocabulary exploration. The premise for this course is to work from texts, tasks, and topics rather than from a structural syllabus in order to generate language and then look for items and patterns. By the end of this course students should be able to express their thoughts on various topics in an orderly and logical fashion, showing a higher degree of comfort with the Portuguese Language to that expressed in the previous basic courses. Emphasis will be placed on writing. The language of the course will be Portuguese. This section is offered through the BTAA Course Share Program hosted by UIUC and will be video-conference/Zoom/online taught for participating universities.

sections.sectionText: TOPIC TITLE: "Brazil through AI: Small Projects, Big Questions." This course explores Brazil's language, literature, science, music and more through short, hands-on projects powered by AI. Every project focuses on Brazil, but the methods apply to any language, culture or field of study. INSTRUCTION IN ENGLISH. KNOWLEDGE OF PORTUGUESE OR CODING NOT REQUIRED.

sections.sectionText: Title: Brazilian Film Brazilian cinema has gained international recognition since the 1960s, particularly through the work of directors like Glauber Rocha, Helena Solberg, and others in the “cinema novo” (New Cinema) movement. This course offers an overview of Brazilian moving images, from the expansion of the national film industry in the 1930s to the digital and streaming age of the 2020s. We will look at cinema as not only an aesthetic medium in its own right, but also as a lens that magnifies and mirrors broader cultural, economic, and political circumstances. Brazilian cinema offers insights into the country’s past and present-day while Brazilian cultural and historical formation enriches our understanding of its cinema. In addition to “cinema novo,” the course will explore a range of styles that include the chanchada (popular comedy), the cinema marginal (Marginal Cinema), the “retomada” (resurgence) of the 1990s, the “pós-retomada” (post-resurgence) in the 2000s, and the “novíssimo” (newest) turn since the 2010s. TAUGHT IN ENGLISH.

Topic Title:Discovering Language and Culture in Digital Worlds. This course examines the language and cultures of online spaces, from multiplayer games and livestreaming communities to forums and text-based worlds. Students will explore a community firsthand, share their environments with their fellow students, and develop a research proposal based on what they discover
